sanskrit: mahāsenety evam uktvā nivṛttaḥ saha daivataiḥ anujñāto bhagavatā tryambakena śacīpatiḥ
english: Having said thus 'O Mahāsena,' Śacīpati turned back together with the gods, having been permitted by the blessed Three-eyed Lord.

sanskrit: gato bhadravaṭaṃ rudro nivṛttāś ca divaukasaḥ uktāś ca devā rudreṇa skandaṃ paśyata mām iva
english: Rudra departed to Bhadravaṭa, and the heavenly dwellers withdrew; and Rudra said to the gods: 'Behold Skanda even as you behold me.'

sanskrit: sa hatvā dānavagaṇān pūjyamāno maharṣibhiḥ ekāhnaivājayat sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ vahninandanaḥ
english: He, the son of Fire, slaying the hosts of Dānavas and being worshipped by the great sages, conquered the entire three worlds in a single day.

sanskrit: skandasya ya idaṃ janma paṭhate susamāhitaḥ sa puṣṭim iha saṃprāpya skandasālokyatām iyāt
english: Whoever reads this birth-story of Skanda with concentrated mind shall gain prosperity in this world and attain to the same realm as Skanda.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca upāsīneṣu vipreṣu pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu draupadī satyabhāmā ca viviśāte tadā samam jāhasyamāne suprīte sukhaṃ tatra niṣīdatuḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the Brāhmaṇas sat in attendance and the great-souled Pāṇḍavas were present, Draupadī and Satyabhāmā entered together at that time; delighting in laughter and deeply pleased, they sat there comfortably.

sanskrit: cirasya dṛṣṭvā rājendra te 'nyonyasya priyaṃvade kathayām āsatuś citrāḥ kathāḥ kuruyadukṣitām
english: O king of kings, having met after a long time, those two sweet-spoken ones told each other varied tales of the Kurus' sorrows.

sanskrit: athābravīt satyabhāmā kṛṣṇasya mahiṣī priyā sātrājitī yājñasenīṃ rahasīdaṃ sumadhyamā
english: Then Satyabhāmā, the beloved queen of Kṛṣṇa, daughter of Satrājit, the slender-waisted one, privately said this to Yājñasenī:

sanskrit: kena draupadi vṛttena pāṇḍavān upatiṣṭhasi lokapālopamān vīrān yūnaḥ paramasaṃmatān kathaṃ ca vaśagās tubhyaṃ na kupyanti ca te śubhe
english: 'By what conduct, Draupadī, do you attend upon the Pāṇḍavas — those heroes equal to guardians of the worlds, young men held in highest esteem? How are they submissive to you and do not grow angry with you, O auspicious one?'

sanskrit: tava vaśyā hi satataṃ pāṇḍavāḥ priyadarśane mukhaprekṣāś ca te sarve tattvam etad bravīhi me
english: 'For the Pāṇḍavas are ever obedient to you, O lovely one, and they all look to your face — tell me the truth of this.'

sanskrit: vratacaryā tapo vāpi snānamantrauṣadhāni vā vidyāvīryaṃ mūlavīryaṃ japahomas tathāgadāḥ
english: 'Is it through vows, austerities, bathing, mantras, or medicines, or through the power of knowledge, the potency of roots, recitation, fire-offerings, or herbal charms?'

sanskrit: mama ācakṣva pāñcāli yaśasyaṃ bhagavedanam yena kṛṣṇe bhaven nityaṃ mama kṛṣṇo vaśānugaḥ
english: 'Tell me, O Pāñcālī, that glorious and blessed knowledge by which Kṛṣṇa might forever remain submissive to me.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā satyabhāmā virarāma yaśasvinī pativratā mahābhāgā draupadī pratyuvāca tām
english: Having spoken thus, Satyabhāmā fell silent; then the illustrious, devoted Draupadī, greatly blessed, replied to her.

sanskrit: asatstrīṇāṃ samācāraṃ satye mām anupṛcchasi asadācarite mārge kathaṃ syād anukīrtanam
english: 'O Satyā, you ask me about the conduct of wicked women — how could I praise a path that is wrongly trodden?'

sanskrit: anupraśnaḥ saṃśayo vā naitat tvayy upapadyate tathā hy upetā buddhyā tvaṃ kṛṣṇasya mahiṣī priyā
english: 'Such a question or doubt does not become you, for you are endowed with wisdom and are the beloved queen of Kṛṣṇa.'

sanskrit: yadaiva bhartā jānīyān mantramūlaparāṃ striyam udvijeta tadaivāsyāḥ sarpād veśmagatād iva
english: 'The very moment a husband learns that his wife relies on spells and roots, he would recoil from her as from a serpent that has entered the house.'

sanskrit: udvignasya kutaḥ śāntir aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham na jātu vaśago bhartā striyāḥ syān mantrakāraṇāt
english: 'Where is peace for an anxious man, and where is happiness for a restless one? A husband can never be made submissive to a woman through sorcery.'

sanskrit: amitraprahitāṃś cāpi gadān paramadāruṇān mūlapravādair hi viṣaṃ prayacchanti jighāṃsavaḥ
english: 'Those who wish to kill administer poison through claims of roots, and also send most terrible diseases dispatched by enemies.'

sanskrit: jihvayā yāni puruṣas tvacā vāpy upasevate tatra cūrṇāni dattāni hanyuḥ kṣipram asaṃśayam
english: 'Powders mixed into what a man consumes with his tongue or applies to his skin kill quickly, without doubt.'

sanskrit: jalodarasamāyuktāḥ śvitriṇaḥ palitās tathā apumāṃsaḥ kṛtāḥ strībhir jaḍāndhabadhirās tathā
english: 'By women have men been made bloated with dropsy, leprous, prematurely grey, impotent, dull-witted, blind, and deaf.'

sanskrit: pāpānugās tu pāpās tāḥ patīn upasṛjanty uta na jātu vipriyaṃ bhartuḥ striyā kāryaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: 'Those wicked women, followers of sin, afflict their husbands — but a woman should never under any circumstances do what is displeasing to her husband.'

sanskrit: vartāmy ahaṃ tu yāṃ vṛttiṃ pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu tāṃ sarvāṃ śṛṇu me satyāṃ satyabhāme yaśasvini
english: 'But hear from me the true conduct I practise toward the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, O glorious Satyabhāmā.'

sanskrit: ahaṃkāraṃ vihāyāhaṃ kāmakrodhau ca sarvadā sadārān pāṇḍavān nityaṃ prayatopacarāmy aham
english: 'Laying aside pride, desire, and anger always, I attend upon the Pāṇḍavas together with their wives, ever striving carefully.'

sanskrit: praṇayaṃ pratisaṃgṛhya nidhāyātmānam ātmani śuśrūṣur nirabhīmānā patīnāṃ cittarakṣiṇī
english: 'Restraining affectation, placing myself within myself, I serve without arrogance, guarding my husbands' hearts.'

sanskrit: durvyāhṛtāc chaṅkamānā duḥsthitād duravekṣitāt durāsitād durvrajitād iṅgitādhyāsitād api
english: 'I am wary of harsh speech, improper posture, unseemly looks, sitting wrongly, walking improperly, and even dwelling on gestures.

sanskrit: sūryavaiśvānaranibhān somakalpān mahārathān seve cakṣurhaṇaḥ pārthān ugratejaḥpratāpinaḥ
english: 'I serve the Pārthas who are like the sun and fire, moon-like in their grace, great warriors whose fierce energy blinds the eyes.

sanskrit: devo manuṣyo gandharvo yuvā cāpi svalaṃkṛtaḥ dravyavān abhirūpo vā na me 'nyaḥ puruṣo mataḥ
english: 'No other man — god, human, or gandharva, though young and well adorned, wealthy or handsome — is regarded by me.

sanskrit: nābhuktavati nāsnāte nāsaṃviṣṭe ca bhartari na saṃviśāmi nāśnāmi sadā karmakareṣv api
english: 'When my husband has not eaten, not bathed, not rested — I do not lie down, do not eat; the same applies always to the servants too.

sanskrit: kṣetrād vanād vā grāmād vā bhartāraṃ gṛham āgatam pratyutthāyābhinandāmi āsanenodakena ca
english: 'When my husband arrives home from field, forest, or village, I rise to welcome him with a seat and water.

sanskrit: pramṛṣṭabhāṇḍā mṛṣṭānnā kāle bhojanadāyinī saṃyatā guptadhānyā ca susaṃmṛṣṭaniveśanā
english: 'I keep vessels scoured, food clean, serve meals on time, am self-restrained, guard the grain, and keep the dwelling well swept.

sanskrit: atiraskṛtasaṃbhāṣā duḥstriyo nānusevatī anukūlavatī nityaṃ bhavāmy analasā sadā
english: 'I do not speak disrespectfully, do not associate with wicked women, am ever agreeable, and never idle.

sanskrit: anarme cāpi hasanaṃ dvāri sthānam abhīkṣṇaśaḥ avaskare cirasthānaṃ niṣkuṭeṣu ca varjaye
english: 'Laughing without occasion, standing repeatedly at the door, lingering at the rubbish-heap, and loitering in the garden-court — these I avoid.

sanskrit: atihāsātiroṣau ca krodhasthānaṃ ca varjaye niratāhaṃ sadā satye bhartṝṇām upasevane sarvathā bhartṛrahitaṃ na mameṣṭaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: 'I avoid excessive laughter, excessive anger, and all occasions of wrath; I am ever devoted, O Satyā, to the service of my husbands; being without a husband is in no way dear to me under any circumstances.

sanskrit: yadā pravasate bhartā kuṭumbārthena kena cit sumanovarṇakāpetā bhavāmi vratacāriṇī
english: 'When a husband travels away on some family business, I become one who observes vows, stripped of flowers and cosmetics.

sanskrit: yac ca bhartā na pibati yac ca bhartā na khādati yac ca nāśnāti me bhartā sarvaṃ tad varjayāmy aham
english: 'Whatever my husband does not drink, whatever he does not chew, whatever he does not eat — all that I also abstain from.

sanskrit: yathopadeśaṃ niyatā vartamānā varāṅgane svalaṃkṛtā suprayatā bhartuḥ priyahite ratā
english: 'Conducting myself in accordance with instruction, restrained, O lovely-limbed one, adorned and ever diligent, I am devoted to my husband's pleasure and welfare.

sanskrit: ye ca dharmāḥ kuṭumbeṣu śvaśrvā me kathitāḥ purā bhikṣābaliśrāddham iti sthālīpākāś ca parvasu mānyānāṃ mānasatkārā ye cānye viditā mayā
english: 'The household duties taught to me long ago by my mother-in-law — almsgiving, offerings to spirits, ancestral rites, ritual pot-cooking at the fortnightly festivals, proper honouring of those worthy of honour, and whatever else I have learned —

sanskrit: tān sarvān anuvartāmi divārātram atandritā vinayān niyamāṃś cāpi sadā sarvātmanā śritā
english: 'All these I follow day and night without fatigue, ever resorting with my whole being to the rules of propriety and restraint.

sanskrit: mṛdūn sataḥ satyaśīlān satyadharmānupālinaḥ āśīviṣān iva kruddhān patīn paricarāmy aham
english: 'I wait upon my husbands — gentle, virtuous, of truthful character, upholders of truth and duty — as upon angry venomous serpents.

sanskrit: patyāśrayo hi me dharmo mataḥ strīṇāṃ sanātanaḥ sa devaḥ sā gatir nānyā tasya kā vipriyaṃ caret
english: 'Reliance on one's husband is the eternal duty of women as I understand it; he is the god, he is the refuge, there is no other — who would do what displeases him?

sanskrit: ahaṃ patīn nātiśaye nātyaśne nātibhūṣaye nāpi parivade śvaśrūṃ sarvadā pariyantritā
english: 'I do not outshine my husbands, do not eat to excess, do not over-adorn myself, nor do I speak ill of my mother-in-law — always I keep myself restrained.

sanskrit: avadhānena subhage nityotthānatayaiva ca bhartāro vaśagā mahyaṃ guruśuśrūṣaṇena ca
english: 'Through attentiveness, O auspicious one, through always rising to serve, and through service to the elders, my husbands are made submissive to me.

sanskrit: nityam āryām ahaṃ kuntīṃ vīrasūṃ satyavādinīm svayaṃ paricarāmy ekā snānācchādanabhojanaiḥ
english: 'I always attend in person on noble Kuntī, mother of heroes, speaker of truth, serving her alone with bathing, clothing, and food.

sanskrit: naitām atiśaye jātu vastrabhūṣaṇabhojanaiḥ nāpi parivade cāhaṃ tāṃ pṛthāṃ pṛthivīsamām
english: 'I never outshine her in garments, ornaments, or food, nor do I speak ill of that Pṛthā who is equal to the earth.

sanskrit: aṣṭāv agre brāhmaṇānāṃ sahasrāṇi sma nityadā bhuñjate rukmapātrīṣu yudhiṣṭhiraniveśane
english: 'Eight thousand Brāhmaṇas used to eat daily in the residence of Yudhiṣṭhira, from golden vessels, in the foremost place.

sanskrit: aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi snātakā gṛhamedhinaḥ triṃśaddāsīka ekaiko yān bibharti yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: 'Eighty-eight thousand householder graduates, each attended by thirty maidservants, were maintained by Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: daśānyāni sahasrāṇi yeṣām annaṃ susaṃskṛtam hriyate rukmapātrībhir yatīnām ūrdhvaretasām
english: 'Ten thousand other ascetics of upward-flowing seed had their well-prepared food carried to them in golden vessels.

sanskrit: tān sarvān agrahāreṇa brāhmaṇān brahmavādinaḥ yathārhaṃ pūjayāmi sma pānācchādanabhojanaiḥ
english: 'All those Brāhmaṇas, speakers of the Veda, I used to honour fittingly with drinks, clothing, and food, along with their land-grants.

sanskrit: śataṃ dāsīsahasrāṇi kaunteyasya mahātmanaḥ kambukeyūradhāriṇyo niṣkakaṇṭhyaḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: 'A hundred thousand maidservants of the great-souled son of Kuntī wore conch-shell bangles and armlets, gold neck-pieces, and were finely adorned.

sanskrit: mahārhamālyābharaṇāḥ suvarṇāś candanokṣitāḥ maṇīn hema ca bibhratyo nṛtyagītaviśāradāḥ
english: 'They wore garlands and ornaments of great value, were of golden complexion, anointed with sandal-paste, bearing gems and gold, skilled in dance and song.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ nāma ca rūpaṃ ca bhojanācchādanāni ca sarvāsām eva vedāhaṃ karma caiva kṛtākṛtam
english: 'I knew the name, form, food, and clothing of all of them, and every task of theirs done or undone.

sanskrit: śataṃ dāsīsahasrāṇi kuntīputrasya dhīmataḥ pātrīhastā divārātram atithīn bhojayanty uta
english: 'A hundred thousand maidservants of the wise son of Kuntī, vessels in hand, fed guests day and night.

sanskrit: śatam aśvasahasrāṇi daśa nāgāyutāni ca yudhiṣṭhirasyānuyātram indraprasthanivāsinaḥ
english: 'A hundred thousand horses and a hundred thousand elephants formed the retinue of Yudhiṣṭhira, dweller of Indraprastha.

sanskrit: etad āsīt tadā rājño yan mahīṃ paryapālayat yeṣāṃ saṃkhyāvidhiṃ caiva pradiśāmi śṛṇomi ca
english: 'Such was the household of the king who protected the earth; their number and arrangement I both directed and kept account of.

sanskrit: antaḥpurāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhṛtyānāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ ā gopālāvipālebhyaḥ sarvaṃ veda kṛtākṛtam
english: 'Of all the inner chambers and of all the servants, down to the cowherds and shepherds, I knew everything done and undone.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ rājñaḥ samudayam āyaṃ ca vyayam eva ca ekāhaṃ vedmi kalyāṇi pāṇḍavānāṃ yaśasvinām
english: 'All the income and expenditure, all the revenue of the king — I alone knew it, O auspicious one, of the illustrious Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: mayi sarvaṃ samāsajya kuṭumbaṃ bharatarṣabhāḥ upāsanaratāḥ sarve ghaṭante sma śubhānane
english: 'Having entrusted the entire household to me, those bulls among Bhāratas, all devoted to their duties, strove on, O fair-faced one.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ bhāram āsaktam anādhṛṣyaṃ durātmabhiḥ sukhaṃ sarvaṃ parityajya rātryahāni ghaṭāmi vai
english: 'That burden, incumbent and unassailable by the wicked, I carry diligently day and night, abandoning all ease.

sanskrit: adhṛṣyaṃ varuṇasyeva nidhipūrṇam ivodadhim ekāhaṃ vedmi kośaṃ vai patīnāṃ dharmacāriṇām
english: 'The treasury of my righteous husbands, unassailable like Varuṇa's domain, full of riches like the ocean — I alone knew it.

sanskrit: aniśāyāṃ niśāyāṃ ca sahāyāḥ kṣutpipāsayoḥ ārādhayantyāḥ kauravyāṃs tulyā rātrir ahaś ca me
english: 'In serving the Kauravas, companions in hunger and thirst alike, in daylight and in dark, night and day are equal to me.

sanskrit: prathamaṃ pratibudhyāmi caramaṃ saṃviśāmi ca nityakālam ahaṃ satye etat saṃvananaṃ mama
english: 'I am the first to wake and the last to retire — this is always my practice, O Satyā; this is my winning of my husbands.

sanskrit: etaj jānāmy ahaṃ kartuṃ bhartṛsaṃvananaṃ mahat asatstrīṇāṃ samācāraṃ nāhaṃ kuryāṃ na kāmaye
english: 'This great winning of husbands I know how to accomplish — the conduct of wicked women I neither follow nor desire.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā dharmasahitaṃ vyāhṛtaṃ kṛṣṇayā tadā uvāca satyā satkṛtya pāñcālīṃ dharmacāriṇīm
english: Having heard what Kṛṣṇā had spoken, filled with righteousness, Satyā then, honouring the righteous Pāñcālī, spoke thus:

sanskrit: abhipannāsmi pāñcāli yājñaseni kṣamasva me kāmakāraḥ sakhīnāṃ hi sopahāsaṃ prabhāṣitum
english: 'I am confounded, O Pāñcālī, O Yājñasenī — forgive me; for it is the habit of friends to speak with jesting freedom.'

sanskrit: draupady uvāca imaṃ tu te mārgam apetadoṣaṃ; vakṣyāmi cittagrahaṇāya bhartuḥ yasmin yathāvat sakhi vartamānā; bhartāram ācchetsyasi kāminībhyaḥ
english: Draupadī said: 'Yet I shall tell you this path free of fault for winning your husband's heart — abiding upon it rightly, dear friend, you shall draw your husband away from other women.'

sanskrit: naitādṛśaṃ daivatam asti satye; sarveṣu lokeṣu sadaivateṣu yathā patis tasya hi sarvakāmā; labhyāḥ prasāde kupitaś ca hanyāt
english: 'There is no deity like a husband, O Satyā, in all the worlds among all the gods — from his favour all desires are gained, and when angered he can destroy.'

sanskrit: tasmād apatyaṃ vividhāś ca bhogāḥ; śayyāsanāny adbhutadarśanāni vastrāṇi mālyāni tathaiva gandhāḥ; svargaś ca loko viṣamā ca kīrtiḥ
english: 'Therefore children, varied enjoyments, wonderful beds and seats, garments, garlands, and fragrances, the world of heaven, and fame — all depend on him.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ sukheneha na jātu labhyaṃ; duḥkhena sādhvī labhate sukhāni sā kṛṣṇam ārādhaya sauhṛdena; premṇā ca nityaṃ pratikarmaṇā ca
english: 'Happiness is never obtained through pleasure alone in this world; a virtuous woman obtains joys through suffering — therefore worship Kṛṣṇa with wholehearted friendship, with love always, and with service in return.'

sanskrit: tathāśanaiś cārubhir agryamālyair; dākṣiṇyayogair vividhaiś ca gandhaiḥ asyāḥ priyo 'smīti yathā viditvā; tvām eva saṃśliṣyati sarvabhāvaiḥ
english: 'With fine foods and choice garlands, with gracious attentions and various perfumes — once he knows "she loves me," he will embrace you alone with his whole being.'

sanskrit: śrutvā svaraṃ dvāragatasya bhartuḥ; pratyutthitā tiṣṭha gṛhasya madhye dṛṣṭvā praviṣṭaṃ tvaritāsanena; pādyena caiva pratipūjaya tvam
english: 'On hearing your husband's voice at the door, rise and stand in the middle of the house; having seen him enter, honour him quickly with a seat and water for his feet.'

sanskrit: saṃpreṣitāyām atha caiva dāsyām; utthāya sarvaṃ svayam eva kuryāḥ jānātu kṛṣṇas tava bhāvam etaṃ; sarvātmanā māṃ bhajatīti satye
english: 'Even when a maidservant has been sent, rise and do everything yourself — let Kṛṣṇa know your disposition, O Satyā: "She serves me with her whole being."'

sanskrit: tvatsaṃnidhau yat kathayet patis te; yady apy aguhyaṃ parirakṣitavyam kā cit sapatnī tava vāsudevaṃ; pratyādiśet tena bhaved virāgaḥ
english: 'What your husband says in your presence — even if not secret — must be guarded; should some rival wife report it back to Vāsudeva, that would cause estrangement.'

sanskrit: priyāṃś ca raktāṃś ca hitāṃś ca bhartus; tān bhojayethā vividhair upāyaiḥ dveṣyair apakṣair ahitaiś ca tasya; bhidyasva nityaṃ kuhakoddhataiś ca
english: 'Those who are dear, devoted, and beneficial to your husband, feed them by various means; from his enemies, partisans against him, and those harmful to him, separate yourself always, by stratagems and outright rejection.'

sanskrit: madaṃ pramādaṃ puruṣeṣu hitvā; saṃyaccha bhāvaṃ pratigṛhya maunam pradyumnasāmbāv api te kumārau; nopāsitavyau rahite kadā cit
english: 'Abandoning pride and heedlessness in the company of men, restrain your feelings, embracing silence; even the young princes Pradyumna and Sāmba must never be waited on by you in a secluded place.'

sanskrit: mahākulīnābhir apāpikābhiḥ; strībhiḥ satībhis tava sakhyam astu caṇḍāś ca śauṇḍāś ca mahāśanāś ca; caurāś ca duṣṭāś capalāś ca varjyāḥ
english: 'Let your friendships be with women of noble birth, sinless, and virtuous; the violent, the drunkards, the gluttons, thieves, the wicked, and the fickle are to be avoided.'

sanskrit: etad yaśasyaṃ bhagavedanaṃ ca; svargyaṃ tathā śatrunibarhaṇaṃ ca mahārhamālyābharaṇāṅgarāgā; bhartāram ārādhaya puṇyagandhā
english: 'This is glorious and conducive to blessed knowledge, celestial and destructive of enemies — adorned with choice garlands and ornaments, fragrant with holy perfumes, worship your husband.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca mārkaṇḍeyādibhir vipraiḥ pāṇḍavaiś ca mahātmabhiḥ kathābhir anukūlābhiḥ sahāsitvā janārdanaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having sat together in pleasant conversation with Mārkaṇḍeya and other sages and with the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, Janārdana —

sanskrit: tatas taiḥ saṃvidaṃ kṛtvā yathāvan madhusūdanaḥ ārurukṣū rathaṃ satyām āhvayām āsa keśavaḥ
english: — then Madhusūdana, having taken proper leave of them, wishing to mount his chariot, Keśava summoned Satyā.

sanskrit: satyabhāmā tatas tatra svajitvā drupadātmajām uvāca vacanaṃ hṛdyaṃ yathābhāvasamāhitam
english: Satyabhāmā then embraced the daughter of Drupada and spoke heartfelt words composed with sincere feeling:

sanskrit: kṛṣṇe mā bhūt tavotkaṇṭhā mā vyathā mā prajāgaraḥ bhartṛbhir devasaṃkāśair jitāṃ prāpsyasi medinīm
english: 'O Kṛṣṇā, let there be no longing in you, no anguish, no sleeplessness — you shall regain the earth won by husbands who are equal to the gods.'

sanskrit: na hy evaṃ śīlasaṃpannā naivaṃ pūjitalakṣaṇāḥ prāpnuvanti ciraṃ kleśaṃ yathā tvam asitekṣaṇe
english: 'For women endowed with such virtue, bearing such auspicious marks, do not suffer long as you do now, O dark-eyed one.'
